newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond new issues come to grinding halt.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond new issues come to grinding halt.

text.p: Corporate bond new issue activity has come to a grinding halt amid the bulk of new Treasury supply and an upcoming Presidents Day holiday, dealers said.

"The word of the day in the new issue market is - "boring" and "dull," said one syndicate source, "with heavy Treasury supply coming in along with the typical slowdown that occurs before a holiday weekend."
The U.S. Treasury auctioned $12.0 billion in 10-year notes on Wednesday at an average yield of 6.374 percent. The Treasury will sell $10 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday.
On Friday, the U.S. credit market will see a shortened trading session, ending at 1400 EST/1900 GMT, ahead of Monday's Presidents Day holiday when U.S. credit and financial markets will be closed.
"It's very quiet...everyone seems to be waiting out the refunding, and watching the stock market as it nears 7,000," another syndicate source said.
Meanwhile, players said the only issue being talked about on Thursday is Colombia's $1.0 billion global two-part debt offering which may price as early as today.
The first tranche consists of $750 million in 10-year global bonds with price talk seen between 130-135 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
The second tranche consist of $250 million of a 30-year issue with price talk in the area of 170 to 175 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.
The deal, which will be jointly lead by underwriters Merrill Lynch & Co and JP Morgan Securities, was boosted in size from an initial $750 million to meet investor demand.

Among upcoming deals in the private placement market, Unifi Communications is expected to set $125 million in seven-year 144A notes via sole manager Smith Barney, sources said. Price talk on the deal is 14 percent.
Globalstar LP is also expected to tap the market with $250 million in 144A notes due 2004 via Lehman Brothers. Price talk is seen in the 11.50 percent area, sources said.
TCI Satellite Entertainment is expected to bring $350 million in a 144A two-part debt offering via joint lead managers Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities and Merrill Lynch & Co, sources said.
The first tranche will consist of $150 million in senior subordinated notes due 2007. Price talk is between 10.75 and 11 percent, sources said.
The second tranche is for $200 million (proceeds) in senior subordinated discount notes due 2007. Price talk is in the 11.75 to 12 percent area, sources added.
Another $150 million in 144A senior subordinated notes is expected to come to market from Sun Media. Price talk is seen at between 9.625 - 9.75 percent, sources said.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is up 5/32 at 97-16/32 to yield 6.69 percent.
